name: Emeritus of Woe // Demonic Tutor
oracle_text:
This creature enters prepared. (While it's prepared, you may cast a copy of its spell. Doing so unprepares it.)
At the beginning of your end step, if two or more creatures died this turn, this creature becomes prepared.
blocked_sentences: This creature enters prepared. (While it's prepared, you may cast a copy of its spell. Doing so unprepares it.)
At the beginning of your end step, if two or more creatures died this turn, this creature becomes prepared.

needs.what: a per-permanent 'prepared' state that is itself a standing casting permission: while a permanent you control is prepared, you may cast a copy of that card's *other castable face* (here the {1}{B} sorcery half of a Creature // Sorcery card) from the battlefield, paying that face's own cost at that face's own timing, with the permanent staying on the battlefield, and the act of casting it clearing the state
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Every piece the engine has is one step off. `second_face`/`second_face_zone` already model a second castable face, but the zone is `Literal["hand", "graveyard"]` -- split and Adventure halves cast from hand, Aftermath from the graveyard -- and there is no battlefield option, which is the only zone prepared ever casts from. `cast_copy` is an *effect op*: it runs during a resolution somebody else started, copies the ability's own source card, and puts the copy on the stack for free via `put_copy_on_stack`; prepared is instead a player-initiated cast of the other face at its printed cost, offered every time the player has priority at sorcery speed, so it belongs to the legal-actions enumerator and not to any op. `play_exiled`/`cast_for_free` is the nearest cast permission and is wrong twice over: it casts one specific card out of exile without paying, not a copy of a face of a permanent on the battlefield for its cost. The static permissions are all lands (`play_lands_from_graveyard`, `play_lands_from_library_top`); none of them offers a spell, and none is scoped to a face of the permanent it sits on

needs.what: an effect that turns the prepared state on -- 'this creature becomes prepared' from a triggered ability, and 'this creature enters prepared' as an enters-with characteristic in the same slot enters-tapped occupies -- plus the matching turn-off used when the copy is cast ('doing so unprepares it')
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `set_flag` writes an arbitrary word onto a permanent and `has_flag` reads it back, which is exactly how renown is stored, but a flag is inert bookkeeping: nothing in the casting-permission path consults `obj.flags`, so a permanent flagged 'prepared' would gain no ability to cast anything and the card would silently do nothing. `set_flag` is also one-way by design -- there is no clear/remove counterpart in `ops`, and `set_turn_flag` expires at the turn boundary rather than on use -- so even a flag-backed implementation could not express 'doing so unprepares it', which is what stops the copy being cast every turn for ever
